m1.title: Make the script probe inspect positional path arguments
m1.imperative:
Change `_probe_script` in scripts/generate_spine.py so it also inspects
POSITIONAL arguments, not only `--flag` tokens.

The rule, and get it exactly right -- this is the whole difficulty:

  * A positional argument that looks like a repo-relative path (it contains a
    `/` or ends in a known file suffix) and contains NO resolver-owned token
    must EXIST under the repo root. If it does not, that is a fault, named,
    with the path and the script.
  * A positional argument that DOES contain a resolver-owned token
    (`epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/dispatch-proof`, `/home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/c2-generate-the-spine`, `<*-skill-dir>`, `<*-session-id>` -- match
    with `init_work_area._RESOLVER_OWNED_TOKEN_RE`, imported, never
    re-declared) is SKIPPED. It cannot be checked before the resolver runs,
    and the resolver is what fills it. This is not "undecidable"; the token
    family is known-good by construction, which is exactly why
    validate_spine.py already accepts it.
  * A positional argument that is not path-shaped at all is left alone.

If you get the second rule wrong, `specs/reviewer.spine.toml` stops generating
-- its `r6-fowler` check passes `.agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/dispatch-proof/FOWLER_PASS.json`, a
positional path whose token is unresolved at generation time. Turning a check
that could not fail into one that cannot pass is the exact defect this whole
epic exists to find. Regenerate BOTH role specs after your change and confirm
they still emit and still validate clean:

    python scripts/generate_spine.py specs/implementer.spine.toml --out .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/generated/implementer.spine.json --root .
    python scripts/generate_spine.py specs/reviewer.spine.toml --out .agent-work/epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/generated/reviewer.spine.json --root .

Add tests to the existing `TestScriptProbe` class in
tests/test_generate_spine.py, following the three-way shape already there:
VIOLATING fixtures the probe must catch (a wrong positional path), INNOCENT
ones it must not (a real positional path; a positional path carrying
`epic-559/c2-generate-the-spine/dispatch-proof`), and keep the accepted-false-alarm case intact.

SECOND, SMALLER TASK, found by the Commander while authoring this very spec.
A malformed `claim` crashes the compiler instead of being refused by name: an
author who writes `[[gate.claim]]` (array-of-tables) where the format wants
`[gate.claim]` (a table) gets

    AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'

out of `compile_spec` at the `(g.get("claim") or {}).get("magnitude")` line,
with a traceback and no fault code. The spec-shape layer never type-checks
`claim`. Add a named spec-shape fault for it -- a `claim` that is not a table,
or carries a `magnitude` outside {normal, large}, or is `large` with no `text`
-- so the author gets a refusal that names the gate and the mistake, in the
same shape as every other spec-shape fault. Pin it with a test. A generator
whose own error path is a traceback is the shape this mission exists to remove.

Update DESIGN_NOTE.md section 4's `script` entry, section 7's fault list, and
section 10's residual row to state what is now covered and what still is not.

Do not modify scripts/validate_spine.py or scripts/checklist_engine.py. Do not
edit any shipped template under skills/*/templates/. Do not run
scripts/install_constellation.py. Do not commit and do not push -- the
Commander integrates.

Attest p1 BEFORE `start m1`: the engine refuses to start a gate whose
precondition is unmet, and the refusal is non-destructive -- attest, then retry.
